title: Graceful regional drain and KV-cache rehydrate playbook
content:
Purpose and scope:
This is a working playbook for orchestrating a graceful drain of an affected region and ensuring KV-cache (prefix/KV caches) are rehydrated in the standby region(s) to avoid severe cold-cache spikes. Focus areas: coordinated DNS TTL adjustments, staged traffic shift percentages, pre-seed strategies for KV cache and edge caches, and operational knobs for rollback.

Context / when to use:
- Partial region degradation (latency or egress saturation) where capacity in-region is insufficient but other regions are healthy.
- Planned maintenance that requires draining traffic with minimal user-visible latency spikes.
- Pre-failure warm-standby priming when telemetry indicates an imminent outage (egress peering loss, inter-region latency spike).

High-level goals:
1) Avoid large P99 latency spikes due to all-requests cold KV-cache misses.
2) Keep request success rate > 99.5% during shift where possible.
3) Limit egress bursts and protect downstream third-party quotas.
4) Make shifts reversible with recorded decision points.

Operator checklist (fast reference):
- Notify SRE channel and paging list: #sre-region-ops and oncall pager. Include time, affected region, and initial plan.
- Confirm telemetry: region health dashboard, backend availability, and queue lengths.
- Identify target standby region(s) and confirm capacity and model variant compatibility.
- Set DNS TTL to 30s (if currently > 60s) for affected routes (see DNS changes section).
- Begin KV-cache pre-seed (see pre-seed steps).
- Execute traffic shift: 5% -> 20% -> 50% -> 100% windows with 5–10 minute observation periods.
- Monitor: token latency P50/P95/P99, error budget burn, KV-cache hit ratio, queue size, and egress metrics.
- If metrics degrade beyond thresholds, rollback to previous step and notify stakeholders.

Decision thresholds (suggested):
- Continue to next step if P95 latency delta < 20% and error rate < 0.5% absolute increase.
- Halt/rollback if P99 latency delta > 30% or error rate increase > 1.5% absolute.
- If KV-cache hit ratio falls below 40% after shift, pause and run targeted rewarm.

Detailed steps:
1) Initial triage and classification
   - Confirm scope: control plane errors vs network egress vs GPU saturation.
   - If control-plane-only anomalies (e.g., management plane), prefer local fixes over full regional drain.
   - If serving node eviction or egress peering loss, proceed with this playbook.

2) Communications
   - Post an incident stub to #sre-region-ops with timeline and plan.
   - Alert Customer Success if sustained degradation expected > 30 minutes.
   - Create a short DRI note in the incident doc: who executes each shift and who authorizes next stage.

3) Prepare the standby region(s)
   - Verify model binaries/variants present and compatible. Check model version pins.
   - Confirm autoscaler targeting and reservation in Dedicated pools.
   - Confirm key management (KMS/HSM) access in target region.

4) KV-cache pre-seed options (choose based on workload):
   - Prefix warm: replay top N prefixes from recent telemetry into target region to fill KV entries for common prompts. Use sample size 1k–5k depending on memory.
   - Synthetic rewarm: run synthetic traces modeled on production prompts at very low QPS but high variety to pre-populate caches.
   - Targeted user sessions: if high-value customers are affected, prewarm using their recent conversation prefixes (with privacy review).
   - Edge/redis warm: if edge caches can be prepopulated, kick small burst of GETs to ensure edge-pop caches have TTLs loaded.

   Notes: Pre-seed early. Start pre-seed before DNS TTL flip by at least 5–10 minutes for large models. Monitor KV fill rate and memory pressure.

5) DNS and routing adjustments
   - Goal: make regional ingress decisions converge quickly while keeping clients able to reach new region.
   - Lower DNS TTL to 30s for affected hostnames. If using service mesh / Anycast, ensure BGP hints are coordinated with networking.
   - For weighted DNS: move 5% weight to standby initially, then progress in steps. For health-checked LB: add standby nodes to pool with minimal weight and increase progressively.
   - For clients with long-lived connections: apply graceful drain on connection layer (keepalive TTL, close new streams only).

6) Progressive traffic shift cadence (example):
   - Step 0: baseline + pre-seed running. Observe 5 minutes.
   - Step 1: 5% shift -> monitor 5–10 minutes.
   - Step 2: 20% shift -> 10 minutes.
   - Step 3: 50% shift -> 10–15 minutes.
   - Step 4: 100% shift (full) -> continue monitoring and decommission nodes gracefully.

7) Telemetry and dashboards to watch (minimum):
   - Routing metrics: weighted distribution by region, DNS query counts and failure rates.
   - Serving metrics: P50/P95/P99 token latency, model GPU queue length, instance CPU/GPU utilization.
   - KV-cache: hit ratio, miss latency, memory pressure, eviction rate.
   - Edge caches: miss ratio at PoP, downstream origin QPS.
   - Upstream egress: third-party rate limits and quota errors.
   - Client-visible errors: request 4xx/5xx breakdown and user-sessions impacted.

Rollback guidance:
- If thresholds breached, immediately step back to the last configuration stable for at least 10 minutes.
- If cannot stabilize at any intermediate step, revert to original region routing and open an incident for dedicated debugging.
- For rollback, prefer reducing traffic in multiples (e.g., 50% -> 20% -> 0) rather than flipping fully to avoid oscillation.

Post-shift recovery / rehydrate after failover
- Keep pre-seed jobs running for 30–60 minutes post-shift to continue improving KV-hit ratios.
- Run rebalancer to move sticky session state if necessary (documented on per-service basis).
- Increase autoscaler cool-down to avoid thrash while caches warm.

Operational pitfalls and notes-to-self:
- TTL coordination: lowering TTL too late results in a large sudden influx when clients finally re-resolve.
- Over-aggressive pre-seed can saturate target egress and push a cascading failure. Cap synthetic rewarm to < 10% expected steady QPS.
- Watch for long-tail clients that do certificate pinning or HTTP connection pinning — they won't re-resolve quickly. Include client-side guidance for major customers when possible.
- Edge PoP warming matters: origin cache warmup isn't enough if PoPs still miss frequently.

Open questions / follow-ups:
- Can we expose a controlled rewarm endpoint that guarantees no billing impact and throttles pre-seed automatically? (Infra/RnD idea)
- Is there a safe universal pre-seed sampler that preserves privacy across multi-tenant traffic? (privacy & legal consult)
- Add an automated traffic-shift orchestrator that ties DNS weight steps to KV-cache hit ratio and latency signals (SRE tooling backlog).

Post-incident checklist (for after completion):
- Write short retro with time-stamped decision log and why each shift step happened. Attach relevant dashboards and links.
- Estimate cost impact from pre-seed and cross-region egress and tag to incident.
- Create follow-up Jira items for any infra or telemetry gaps.
- Update this playbook with any lessons (make note in doc header with date).

Recent run notes (example - 2025-02-10 simulated run)
- We did a simulated drain of us-west-2 -> us-east-1 for 30 minutes. Pre-seed (prefix warm) filled ~72% of hot prefixes in 8 minutes.
- Observed a P99 bump of 12% during the 50% shift which met thresholds.
- Edge PoP misses were dominant source of user-visible latency; follow-up: add PoP-level rewarm step.

Appendix: quick ops command snippets
- Lower DNS TTL (example): gcloud dns record-sets transaction start && gcloud dns record-sets transaction add --ttl=30 <...>
- Kick pre-seed job (k8s): kubectl -n infra jobs/kv-preseed-runner --image="infra/kv-warm:canary" --args="--sample=2000"
- Check KV stats (internal API): curl -sS https://metrics-api.prod.internal/kvcache?region=us-east-1 | jq .hit_ratio

Decision log (sample entries):
- 2025-02-10 14:05 - Evan B: start pre-seed in us-east-1 (auth: Aisha P)
- 2025-02-10 14:16 - Noah K: move weight to 5% (observed no material change)
- 2025-02-10 14:30 - Evan B: move to 50% after confirms KV-hit > 60%

Notes to self:
- Update patient guidance for customers with long-lived TCP connections.
- Add a small demo to the SRE runbook training for prefix pre-seed commands.

Related artifacts and references:
- INF-4721: experiment notes on kvcache pre-seed algorithms.
- Runbook repo PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runbooks/pull/98
- Slack channel: #sre-region-ops for historical incident chat.

End of draft.
